issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock: the problem statement gives conflicting requirements. In the Problem Statement (lines 70-71) SealSaloon.stock is described as a final Stock that should be initialized in the SealSaloon constructor (instance-level, initialized at construction). Later in the Problem Statement (lines 77-81) it explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). The Solution implements a static field: SealSaloon declares 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' (solution file). This contradiction confuses students whether to implement stock as an instance final field initialized in the constructor or as a static class-level final field initialized at declaration; following the earlier instruction and initializing a static field in a constructor would be incorrect and may lead to design or compilation confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent. Prefer one of the two designs and update the text and UML accordingly. Recommended fix to preserve intended shared stock behavior: require a static shared stock and show initialization at declaration. Change the constructor-related instruction to remove 'initialize in the constructor' and instead state: 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' (initialized at declaration). Also remove or update any examples or wording that imply instance-only stock. If the intended design were instance-specific stock, remove the 'static' requirement and keep the constructor initialization instruction.
